parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the table to show the composition and identity of some atoms and ions.

| name of element | nucleon number | atomic number | number of protons | number of neutrons | number of electrons | overall charge |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| boron | 10 | 5 |  |  |  | 0 |
| nitrogen |  |  |  | 8 | 10 |  |
|  | 208 | 82 | 82 |  | 80 |  |
|  |  |  | 3 | 3 |  | +1 |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
The fifth to eighth ionisation energies of three elements in the third period of the Periodic Table are given. The symbols used for reference are **not** the actual symbols of the elements.

|  | ionisation energies, $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |  |  |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| {{blocked}} | fifth | sixth | seventh | eighth |
| **X** | 7012 | 8496 | 27 107 | 31 671 |
| **Y** | 6542 | 9362 | 11 018 | 33 606 |
| **Z** | 7238 | 8781 | 11 996 | 13 842 |
parts.text: State and explain the group number of element **Y**.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain the general trend in **first** ionisation energies across the third period.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Complete the electronic configuration of element **X**.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
A sample of oxygen exists as a mixture of three isotopes. Information about two of these isotopes is given in the table.

| mass number | 16 | 17 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| abundance | $99.76\%$ | $0.04\%$ |
parts.text: Calculate the abundance of the third isotope.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The relative atomic mass of this sample of oxygen is $16.0044$.

Calculate the mass number of the third isotope. You **must** show your working.
